newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electric futures end higher amid cold snap.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electric futures end higher amid cold snap.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures settled up Monday but well off their intraday highs in a choppy session amid stronger cash prices prompted by frigid temperatures across the U.S.
"With this cold snap, we ought to be higher. There was no followthrough," said a Houston marketer.
California-Oregon Border (COB) futures were also bolstered by a rise in Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) prices.

The federal power marketing agency raised its offer price for firm power during heavy load hours on Tuesday to as high as $46.00 per megawatt hour (MWh), nearly tripling the price of offers from late last week.
Peak, firm power values for day-ahead delivery in the West surged to levels similar to BPA's prices.
February COB futures ended up 70 cents at $14.40/MWh after traded between $13.80 and $15.00. March COB finished up 20 cents at $12.40.
February Palo Verde (PV) futures ended up eight cents at $16.53 after bouncing between $16.30 and $17.05. March PV finished up 10 cents at $14.50.
The deep freeze out West was expected to continue at least through midweek.

In the natural gas market, cash and futures prices took opposite direction. NYMEX February Henry Hub futures finished down 6.2 cents at $3.254 per million British thermal units (mmBtu), while swing gas prices in the U.S. Gulf firmed 10 cents near the $4.00/mmBtu level.
In the West, February natgas to the San Juan/Blanco Hub were last quoted at $3.05-$3.15, compared with $3.15-$3.23 Friday.
Some market sources said the electricity complex could turn bearish Tuesday if it fails to extend today's gain.
